questions.subject: NP IV
questions.stem: 'Doing the right thing' rather than 'doing things right' describes:
questions.rationale: Leadership focuses on purpose and the future; management on structure and the present.

questions.quote: Motto Do the right thing I Do things right

questions.subject: NP IV
questions.stem: In Lewin's change theory, staff becoming aware of the need for change is:
questions.rationale: Unfreezing: awareness; moving: working toward change; refreezing: stabilizing.
questions.source: TRA Nursing Module, Lewin's Theory (PDF p. 520)
questions.quote: Development through problem awareness of a need for change.

questions.subject: NP IV
questions.stem: A new protocol becomes part of routine practice. This is which Lewin stage?
questions.rationale: Refreezing integrates and stabilizes the change.
questions.source: TRA Nursing Module, Lewin's Theory (PDF p. 520)
questions.quote: Integration of the change into one's personality and the consequent stabilization of change.

questions.subject: NP IV
questions.stem: Convincing staff with evidence that a change benefits them uses which strategy?
questions.rationale: Empirical-rational assumes people adopt justified changes that benefit them.
questions.source: TRA Nursing Module, Change Strategies (PDF p. 520)
questions.quote: people should be willing to adopt a change if it is justified

questions.subject: NP IV
questions.stem: Change involving mutual goal setting, equal power, and deliberateness is:
questions.rationale: Planned change has mutual goals, equal power, and deliberation.
questions.source: TRA Nursing Module, Types of Change (PDF p. 520)
questions.quote: Involves mutual goal setting, an equal power ratio, and deliberativeness.

questions.subject: NP IV
questions.stem: McClelland's theory identifies needs for achievement, affiliation, and:
questions.rationale: McClelland: achievement, power, affiliation.
questions.source: TRA Nursing Module, Motivation Theories (PDF p. 521)
questions.quote: achievement, power

questions.subject: NP IV
questions.stem: A nurse feels underpaid compared with a colleague doing the same work. Which theory explains her motivation?
questions.rationale: Equity theory: fairness judged by comparing inputs and rewards with others.
questions.source: TRA Nursing Module, Equity Theory (PDF p. 521)
questions.quote: employees assess fairness by considering their input

questions.subject: NP I
questions.stem: A study testing whether breastfeeding reduces infant pain during injections is:

questions.subject: NP I
questions.stem: In 'number of prenatal classes and anxiety about labor,' the dependent variable is:

questions.subject: NP I
questions.stem: Which characteristic describes qualitative research?
questions.rationale: Qualitative: narrative, subjective, inductive, theory development, field setting.

questions.subject: NP I
questions.stem: A true experiment requires manipulation, control, and:

questions.source: TRA Nursing Module, True Experimental Design (PDF p. 523)
questions.quote: Randomization

questions.subject: NP I
questions.stem: A study with an intervention but no random assignment is:
questions.rationale: Quasi-experiments lack randomization.

questions.quote: quasi-experimental designs lack randomization

questions.subject: NP I
questions.stem: In-depth interviews exploring the lived experience of women after pelvic surgery is:

questions.subject: NP I
questions.stem: Studying the health lifeways of an indigenous community through fieldwork is:
questions.rationale: Ethnography studies cultural groups holistically.

questions.quote: studying the patterns, lifeway and experiences of a cultural group

questions.subject: NP I
questions.stem: 'There is no significant relationship between anxiety and duration of infertility' is a:

questions.subject: NP I
questions.stem: Which literature source is most recommended for a review?

questions.quote: Mostly recommended.

questions.subject: NP I
questions.stem: Following premature infants' development from birth through childhood is a:

questions.quote: Premature infants-evaluating development during childhood.

questions.subject: NP I
questions.stem: Selecting every 10th patient from a list is which sampling method?

questions.subject: NP I
questions.stem: Asking early participants to refer others who meet criteria is:

questions.subject: NP I
questions.stem: Staff perform better because they know they are being observed. This is the:

questions.subject: NP I
questions.stem: Levels of anxiety (mild, moderate, severe, panic) are measured on which scale?
questions.rationale: Ordinal ranks categories; nominal only classifies.

questions.quote: E.g. levels of anxiety (mild, moderate, severe and panic)

questions.stem: The most frequently occurring score in a distribution is the:

questions.stem: Rejecting a null hypothesis that is actually true is a:

questions.stem: Using multiple data sources to confirm findings is:
